notes:
I don't have any commentary notes on Ezekiel 21 for you yet. My research didn't get far enough to produce anything you could rely on.

I tried to load six sources in one batch: Enduring Word, the Ellicott, Gill and Pulpit commentaries on BibleHub, Precept Austin and the NET Bible notes. A bug in my own code stopped the script before any page content was displayed. When I tried to inspect what had come back, the tool told me I had no more research calls left for this turn, so I couldn't retry or check which pages had loaded.

So I haven't read anything from any of the sites on your list. Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never to fill gaps from my own knowledge, so I haven't written any verse notes rather than invent content or URLs.

If you send a follow-up message, my tool access should reset and I can start again. I'd do it in this order:
1. **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word, Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit Commentary and Precept Austin.
2. **Differences between Protestant traditions:** I'd focus on the verses where they're likeliest to differ:
   - v. 3–4, the righteous being cut off along with the wicked
   - v. 10 and 13, the obscure "scepter of My son" lines
   - v. 21, the king of Babylon's divination
   - v. 26–27, "until He comes whose right it is," often read as a messianic text
   For these I'd check sources such as Wesley's notes, Spurgeon, Ligonier, Got Questions and the Lutheran sites.
3. **Other views:** NET Bible notes for modern scholarship, New Advent and catholic.com for Catholic readings, and OCA for Orthodox readings. I'd include these only where those pages actually discuss this chapter.
